science.title: Seismic dynamic response and instability failure patterns of fractured, loosened, unloaded rock slopes at Lancang River hydropower station
science.description: Fractured loosened rock masses are widely developed in the shallow subsurface of alpine valleys in southwestern China and are commonly underlain by toppling-deformed rock masses, forming a distinctive layered slope structure of "upper fractured–lower toppling" that poses a prominent instability risk under strong earthquakes. However, existing studies have mostly focused on single-layer or homogeneous rock slopes, and the dynamic response characteristics and instability evolution mechanism of this composite structure remain insufficiently understood. Taking the SL slope of a hydropower station on the Lancang River as the prototype, this study constructs a refined three-dimensional numerical model using 3DEC coupled with a discrete fracture network and performs a full-time-history dynamic analysis. The results show that: (1) The fractured loosened rock mass is the dominant sensitive unit of dynamic response; the vertical PGA amplification coefficient at the slope crest exceeds 3.0 and the horizontal PGA amplification coefficient on the slope surface exceeds 2.0, exhibiting a vertical zonation pattern of "deep attenuation—middle fluctuation—shallow amplification." (2) The slope instability successively undergoes four stages: surficial scattered rockfall (peak velocity 7.32 m/s), middle-layer tensile cracking and sliding (8.16 m/s), toppling-fracture-induced retrogressive movement (9.83 m/s), and whole-layer disintegration failure (13.28 m/s); the core mechanism is the retrogressive overall instability triggered by flexural fracture of the underlying toppling-deformed rock mass. (3) With increasing seismic intensity, the failure mode evolves in a stepwise manner, and three critical thresholds are identified—structural-plane shear strength (0.2 g), toppling-mass flexural strength (0.5 g), and slope-toe shear-through (1.0 g)—corresponding to the evolutionary sequence of "surficial scattered rockfall → middle-layer tensile cracking and sliding → toppling-fracture-induced retrogressive movement → whole-layer disintegration failure."

science.title: Association of acetylcholinesterase inhibitor use with mortality among critically ill patients with sepsis
science.description: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (AChEIs) may modulate systemic inflammation via the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway, but their prognostic significance in sepsis remains unclear. This retrospective cohort study was conducted using real-world intensive care unit (ICU) data and included eligible patients with sepsis. AChEI exposure was defined as any recorded use during the ICU stay, and outcomes were 28-, 90-, and 365-day all-cause mortality. Associations were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression, with inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and time-dependent Cox analyses performed to address confounding and the timing of AChEI initiation. Subgroup and interaction analyses assessed heterogeneity. Prediction models derived from the multivariable models were implemented as a web-based application and evaluated for discrimination, calibration, overall prediction accuracy, clinical utility, and bootstrap internal validation. A total of 28,838 patients with sepsis were included, of whom 4,123 received AChEIs. AChEI use was significantly associated with lower 28-, 90-, and 365-day mortality (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.21–0.30, E-value 7.34; HR 0.26, 95% CI 0.23–0.31, E-value 7.05; and HR 0.27, 95% CI 0.23–0.31, E-value 6.99, respectively), with consistent findings in IPTW-weighted and modified Poisson regression analyses. Time-dependent Cox analyses yielded consistent associations at 28, 90, and 365 days (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.24–0.34; HR 0.29, 95% CI 0.24–0.34; and HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.24–0.33, respectively). Peripherally acting AChEIs (n = 3,769) were associated with lower mortality estimates than centrally acting AChEIs (n = 354) at 28, 90, and 365 days (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.19–0.39; HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.22–0.42; and HR 0.33, 95% CI 0.24–0.45, respectively). Associations were generally consistent across subgroups, with significant interactions for sex, dementia, acute kidney injury, and beta-blocker use. The prediction models showed good discrimination, with C-indices of 0.788, 0.780, and 0.770 for 28-, 90-, and 365-day mortality, respectively, and generally good calibration after bootstrap internal validation. AChEI use showed a significant inverse association with short- and long-term mortality in patients with sepsis, with potential heterogeneity across pharmacological subtypes and certain clinical subgroups. These findings warrant further investigation, while the prediction models require external validation before broader clinical application.

science.title: Combined ethanol and lauromacrogol sclerotherapy for ovarian endometriotic cysts: a retrospective clinical and experimental study
science.description: Ovarian endometriotic cysts can reduce ovarian reserve, and surgery may further damage ovarian tissue. Ultrasound-guided sclerotherapy is a less invasive option, but evidence for combined sclerosants is limited. We retrospectively evaluated 84 women with ovarian endometriotic cysts treated with combined ethanol–lauromacrogol sclerotherapy and performed a complementary mouse experiment to assess short-term changes. One month after treatment, cyst diameter, cyst volume and serum CA-125 were significantly reduced. Serum AMH, FSH and LH did not significantly change, procedural pain was generally mild, and no major procedure-related complications were recorded. AFC increased after treatment, although this may reflect better sonographic visualization after cyst shrinkage rather than improved ovarian function. In mice with OEC-like lesions, ethanol, lauromacrogol, and combined treatment reduced cyst burden within 7 days, but the combined regimen did not demonstrate superiority over either monotherapy. Collagen deposition was lower in treated groups, while serum AMH and CTGF did not differ significantly among groups. These findings suggest that combined ethanol–lauromacrogol sclerotherapy is feasible for selected patients and is associated with short-term cyst reduction without early measurable deterioration in selected ovarian reserve-related markers. Comparative clinical benefit, long-term recurrence control, and reproductive safety remain unestablished and require prospective controlled studies with longer follow-up.

science.title: Protocatechuic acid inhibits high shear stress-induced platelet adhesion and aggregation through the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway
science.description: High shear stress in stenotic arteries triggers platelet activation and aggregation, contributing to atherosclerosis and thrombus formation. Protocatechuic acid (PCA), a polyphenol metabolite, has been reported to inhibit shear-induced platelet aggregation (SIPA), but its precise mechanism remains unclear. We aimed to elucidate the mechanism by which PCA inhibits SIPA via the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway. A stenotic microfluidic chip model was used to simulate pathological high shear conditions (10,000 s−1). Platelet aggregation and activation were assessed, and the impact of PCA (51.91 μmol/L) on SIPA was evaluated. Flow cytometry was used to quantify platelet surface markers (using P-selectin and PAC-1 as indicators). Platelet morphology was examined via scanning electron microscopy. Platelet aggregation status was observed through electron microscopy. Western blotting was performed to assess PI3K/Akt signaling pathway proteins. PCA inhibited SIPA across the studied concentration range. At 51.91 μmol/L, PCA significantly reduced platelet adhesion and aggregation. Flow cytometry results indicated that PCA significantly inhibited the expression of the platelet activation marker CD62P. Western blot analysis revealed that PCA markedly inhibited PI3K expression and Akt phosphorylation induced by high shear stress. Co-treatment with the PI3K inhibitor TGX221 further enhanced PCA’s inhibitory effect on Akt phosphorylation. PCA suppresses platelet activation and aggregation under high shear stress, likely by inhibiting the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway, highlighting its potential as an antiplatelet agent.
